summary: Sound stage-1 port of a kernel that already beat FA3+combine+norm-gate in muse_attention_decode (22.8 -> 18.6 us kernel time, shape 27.19 -> 22.6). Run it now on current master in parallel with dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl-t1-gate (c6cb53d8); do not wait. Whichever lands second needs an explicit restack that composes the two, because t1-gate's _dl2_attention takes over full decode_1 before master's branch and would make this port dead code. The expected gain is overstated by about 3-5 us.
justification: Mechanism: at full decode_1, master runs unpaired FA3 with scheduler_metadata, then FlashAttnFwdCombine, then FusedRMSNormGate. Profile c243a29f (profile 1): FA3 main 18.5 us, combine 7.0 us, norm-gate in the '7 more' rows (~1-1.5 us). That is ~26.5-27 us of attention for 20.5 MB of FP8 KV, against a ~4.3 us floor. The source kernel (splitkv_attn_sk_kernel<4,true,true>, grid = SM count, two-level ticket, fused v_scale + norm-gate epilogue) measured 18.6 us in attention profile 2a324178. There it replaced FA3 14.7 + combine 7.0 + norm-gate 1.1. It passed 16/16 tests, including graph replay and the ticket reset. So M1 is likely, and M2 (<= 20 us replaced chain) is plausible. Shape weight: full decode_1 is weight 16. Directions for decode_16/32, sliding and verify are flat by the config gate (batch == 1, window == 0, q_len 1, page 1), which is consistent. WEAKEST LINK: the savings arithmetic. (1) The 'elementwise 3.0 us (3 calls)' row is not pad/unpad. Master pairs only at batch > 1, so batch 1 has no pad/unpad copies. Those 3 calls are the q/k/v FP8 casts before store_cache and FA3, and the new path still needs them (the split-KV route itself does q.to(FP8).contiguous()). So the replaced set is ~26.5-27 us, not ~30. (2) FA3 main runs 18.5 us inside decode_layer vs 14.7 us standalone, so the layer environment (L2 flushed by ~150 MB of weights, a different launch neighbour) costs ~25% here. The SK kernel will likely pay a similar tax, ~19-23 us, not 18.6. Realistic shape: 142.7 -> ~135-138 us (-5 to -8 us), not ~132. The kill line (not faster than 140 at z >= 2, err ~0.57 us) is still a fair test. Stage-1 caveat: 18.6 us for 20.5 MB is ~1.1 TB/s, about 4x off the floor, so M3 is far away. The attention review already named grid = SM count (1 CTA/SM and ~9.5 tiles each, prologue-dominated) as the open tuning knob.
confounders: full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl (master b047510): it owns _splitkv_gate, the v1 module (kernels A/B) and the unpaired-q route at 1 < batch <= 64. The port extends the q preparation to batch 1 and adds a second CUDA module (the attention v3 TU). If the builder edits _splitkv_gate or the shared q route rather than adding a separate batch-1 predicate, decode_16/32 could move. Their expected-flat rows (306.7 / 479.6 us) are the guard. Any movement there is a build defect, not an effect of this hypothesis.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (master): at T=1 the attention output goes to the nvjet o GEMM, then attn_boundary, then the PDL chain (P, R, Marlin). The SK kernel ends with a serialized last-group merge on one CTA (~1-2 us tail). Nothing PDL-launched follows it directly, so no overlap changes. Read the attention rows, not the headline, because P/Marlin rows at decode_1 vary by ~1 us between runs.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched (master): pairing needs batch > 1, so batch 1 is already unpaired. The new branch must sit before the paired/FA3 else-branch and keep 'paired' false at batch 1. No confound if it does.
sliding-decode1-fused / stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 (master): sliding and T>32 only. The sliding decode_1 row (126.2 us) is an in-run drift control for the target row.

IN FLIGHT, not landed: dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl-t1-gate (job c6cb53d8ebc2478a). At full T=1 only, it routes kernel_fn through _dl2_attention: Q = dl_qkv_kernel (qkv GEMV + QK-norm + FP8 q + cache store), then FA3, then O = dl_o_kernel, whose prologue does the RMSNorm x sigmoid(gate) and which fuses the o GEMM. Both hypotheses claim FusedRMSNormGate at full decode_1. t1-gate also removes the 3 FP8 casts. Because it is not on master, it does not confound this run's measurement. It does change landing: its predicate fires before master's attention branch, so after it lands a port built on master would be bypassed silently at full decode_1. The gains are sub-additive by ~1-1.5 us (both remove the norm-gate).
interference: No companion. This is kind: rewrite, stage 1. Its own replaced-kernel rows decide it: the splitkv_attn_sk_kernel row against FA3 main + FlashAttnFwdCombine + norm-gate in the full decode_1 profile. The same run has two internal controls: the sliding decode_1 row (drift) and full decode_16/32 (master's batch>1 split-KV code, which must be byte-identical). The two sub-decisions (grid SM vs 2xSM, two-level vs single-level ticket) are template or argument switches. The attention build already brackets them with in-process eager diagnostics, so carry the [sk3-diag] printout over. An okc A/B would spend a check to learn what a prepare-time print already shows. WAIT OR STACK vs dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl-t1-gate: run now on master, do not wait. The two runs replace disjoint main kernels (this one FA3 + combine, t1-gate the qkv/o GEMMs and casts), so each attributes cleanly on its own base. Landing rule: whichever lands second must restack onto the new master by hand, and must not be landed from its own patch. If t1-gate lands first, compose at full T=1 as Q(dl_qkv) -> SK two-level (with its norm-gate epilogue) -> dl_o with prologue=False. dl_o_kernel already takes a 'prologue' flag. The alternative is an SK variant without the epilogue feeding dl_o with prologue on. Then re-measure with one check, because the norm-gate saving is counted twice. If this port lands first, t1-gate's _dl2_attention must call the SK path instead of FA3 at full decode_1. If t1-gate has already landed when this is claimed, build on that master with the composition above instead of on today's master. Also coordinate with the queued sibling full-decode-streamk-ticket-port. It ports the same v3 TU for batch > 1, so both should share one module name and one load_inline. Otherwise the second to land carries two copies of splitkv_attn_sk_kernel.
rules_flags: Compile/import budget (15 min per run, prepare <= 300 s): decode_layer already builds _DL_CUDA and the v1 split-KV module. Porting the whole attention v3 TU (4 template variants) plus 12 batch-1 self-check cases, 2 graph replays and the 4-variant B=1 and B=16 diagnostics adds noticeable build and import time. Instantiate only <4,true,true> (and whatever the canary needs), and drop the B=16 diagnostic, which is unused here.

Ticket buffers (ticket[b], gticket[b*32+g]) persist across calls. That is fine because they are zero-initialized, reset in-kernel by the last arrival and not derived from data. The two-replay self-check must assert both levels sum to 0 after the replays, as in the attention build.

The spec says 'no allocation in kernel_fn', but master's _splitkv_attn does allocate (torch.empty under graph capture). Preallocating gacc/gml/partials in prepare() from config is fine and not data-derived. Either form is legal, and the builder should not refactor master's batch>1 allocations to match.

Precision and every-key: unchanged from the source (FP8 E4M3 q, FP8 KV, fp32 partials, bf16 out). Stream-K tiles cover every key of the single request, with no skipping. scheduler_metadata is simply unused on the new path, which is allowed.

Self-check and canary must run in-process (no child process). The prepare-time selector timing must stay outside kernel_fn. The gate must read config only (batch, q_len, window, page, heads), plus a flag set once in prepare.
open_questions: Does the SK kernel pay the same ~25% in-layer tax as FA3 (14.7 standalone -> 18.5 in layer)? If it lands at ~23 us, M2 (<= 20 us) is missed, and stage 2 should be grid 2xSM or a PDL pre-wait prologue (prefetch q/meta and start the KV ring before griddepcontrol.wait) so the KV stream overlaps the qkv GEMM tail.
Builder: put the batch-1 predicate as a separate config gate ahead of the paired/FA3 else-branch, and leave _splitkv_gate (1 < batch <= 64) untouched, so decode_16/32 are byte-identical.

Builder: print PATH CHOSEN for full decode_1 and the [sk3-diag] grid/ticket variants at B=1 x 80000 next to master FA3 main + combine + norm-gate at the same input. If the selector's 'new vs incumbent' margin is under ~2 us, say so: the judge undercounts prepare timings by 20-25% (LESSONS).
If dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl-t1-gate gains and lands first, mint the composed restack (Q -> SK -> O prologue=False) as this hypothesis's stage 2 rather than landing this branch as is.
fa3-full-single-split-probe and fa3-num-splits-full-no-metadata (queued, hold) tune FA3 at full decode. If this lands, they no longer apply at batch 1 and should be re-scoped to batch > 1 or retired.
